Gran Gran has a plan: they can use the puddles outside to do a science experiment inside. They use timers and the sun to track the edge of the puddle and find out how long it takes for a puddle to disappear.

programme.title: People's Palaces - The Golden Age of Civic Architecture
programme.desc: S1 E1 — Neo-ClassicalJonathan Foyle explores some of the best Georgian and Victorian neoclassical civic buildings, visiting town halls, concert halls, libraries, schools and galleries in Liverpool, Leeds, Bradford, Manchester and Todmorden in an unlikely story of rivalry, ambition and power in the service of social responsibility. Featuring contributions from historians.

programme.title: The Medici: Makers of Modern Art

Within its 311 panels is the entire history of the world.

programme.title: Nations Championship
programme.desc: S1 E25 — France v South AfricaFrance v South Africa (Kick-off 8.10pm). Jill Douglas presents coverage of both teams' second match of the Northern Hemisphere Series, and penultimate contest of the round-robin stage as a whole, held at Stade de France. The Springboks have won nine of the last 10 meetings between the sides, with five of those triumphs coming here, including a 32-17 victory with 14 men when the nations last faced each other 12 months ago. With analysis from Bryan Habana, Benjamin Kayser and Dan Biggar, and commentary by Miles Harrison and Ben Kay.

programme.title: Tomb Raider
programme.desc: Action adventure starring Alicia Vikander and Dominic West. Heiress Lara Croft refuses to believe her father, a famed explorer, is dead. When a mysterious message reaches her, she heads to a remote Japanese island in search of the truth.

programme.title: Lingo
programme.desc: S5 E14The fast-paced game of words hosted by Adil Ray. Taking on the reigning champions are mother and son Rob and Fran and brother and sister-in-law Amanda and Wayne.

programme.title: Deal or No Deal

programme.title: James Martin's French Adventure
programme.desc: Saint-Emilion (Shortened)The chef travels through France to visit the locations that inspired his culinary career, beginning at the Chateau Cheval Blanc in Saint-Emilion, before going back to the kitchens of the Hostellerie de Plaisance, where he worked as a lad more than 30 years ago. He rounds off his trip by cooking at an award-winning vineyard.

programme.title: James Martin's American Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E20 — New YorkThe chef ends his coast-to-coast exploration of the US in New York City. After a bite of pizza at a popular pizzeria in Greenwich Village, James cooks on one of the city's famous piers. New York has a wealth of French fine-dining restaurants, and the chef cannot wait to take a bite of the action. He chooses his favourite pair, Daniel, run by his old mate Daniel Boulud, and Le Bernadine, where Eric Ripart is in charge. At the end of the day, James cooks back on the pier as sunset approaches and he reminisces on his journey of more than 3,000 miles.

programme.title: Love Your Weekend with Alan Titchmarsh
programme.desc: S8 E29Joining Alan at Manor Farm this Remembrance Sunday are former racing driver Billy Monger and actress Laura Aikman. Plus, a celebration of the role of donkeys during the world wars, and the D-Day Darlings perform a Vera Lynn classic.

programme.title: ITV News
programme.desc: E87 — 14/11/2026A round-up of the latest headlines.

programme.title: James Martin's Saturday Morning
programme.desc: S9 E35James is joined by actress Shelley Conn, who is starring in ITV1's Adultery. The comedian and travel writer Dom Joly is also in the house, with chefs Sally Abe and Glynn Purnell. James cooks Thai green curry and Spanish tapas.

programme.title: Nations Championship
programme.desc: Italy v ArgentinaItaly v Argentina (Kick-off 11.40am). Lauren Salter presents all the action from the Northern Hemisphere Series match at Stadio Comunale Luigi Ferraris in Genoa. Argentina have won the last nine meetings between the sides, with the most recent of those victories an emphatic 50-18 victory in Udine two years ago. With commentary by Nick Heath and Nolli Waterman, and analysis from Jamie Roberts and Sam Warburton.

programme.title: Nations Championship
programme.desc: Wales v New ZealandWales v New Zealand (Kick-off 2.10pm). Lauren Salter presents coverage of the Northern Hemisphere Series match at Principality Stadium in Cardiff. Wales have not defeated the All Blacks since 1953, with New Zealand winning 34 consecutive matches against them since then. The last meeting between the sides came here 12 months ago, when the visitors scored seven tries in a 52-26 triumph. Commentary comes from Gareth Rhys Owen, Shane Williams, and Jamie Roberts, with analysis by Sean Fitzpatrick, Sam Warburton, and Dan Biggar.

programme.title: Nations Championship
programme.desc: England v JapanEngland v Japan (Kick-off 4.40pm). Mark Pougatch presents all the action from the Northern Hemisphere Series match at Allianz Stadium Twickenham. England have won all six of the previous meetings between the nations, including a comfortable 59-14 victory here when the sides last faced each other two years ago, and they will expect to maintain that 100 per cent record today. With commentary by Nick Mullins and David Flatman, analysis from Ugo Monye and Maggie Alphonsi, and reports by Topsy Ojo.

programme.title: Nations Championship
programme.desc: S1 E29 — Ireland v FijiIreland v Fiji (Kick-off 8.10pm). Mark Pougatch presents all the action from the Northern Hemisphere Series match at Aviva Stadium. Ireland boast a 100 per cent record from their eight meetings with Fiji, and comfortably prevailed 52-17 in the most recent of those encounters two years ago, which also took place at this venue. With the Fijians failing to win any of their opening three contests, the Irish will be expecting yet another victory this evening. With commentary by Martin Gillingham and Gordon D'Arcy, analysis from Ugo Monye and Maggie Alphonsi, and reports by Claire Thomas.

Their plight is complicated, however, by the arrival of the mysterious Marcus Wright, a stranger whose purpose is unclear.

programme.title: English Football League Highlights
programme.desc: S5 E18 — 14/11/2026Action from the latest matches, including Stockport County v Reading at Edgeley Park and Wigan Athletic v Barnsley at The Brick Community Stadium in League One.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: S9 E2Geordie receives a call about a dead body at the River View Hotel but when he goes to investigate, Will and Bonnie discover a baby abandoned inside the church wrapped in a blanket from the same hotel. Ernie leads the pair to believe the baby was abandoned by a school girl. Geordie is shocked and upset to hear Will and Bonnie are thinking of leaving Grantchester.

programme.title: Ainsley's Taste of the Bahamas
programme.desc: S1 E2 — From Farm to TableAinsley Harriott explores the Bahamas' home-grown side as he finds out how to grow salad vegetables without soil at Blue Fields, picks ingredients straight from the trees at Chiccharney Farms and discovers the magic of the mangroves. Once back in his beachside kitchen, Ainsley proceeds to cook a whole snapper.

programme.title: Ainsley's Taste of the Bahamas
programme.desc: S1 E3 — Sweet Island LifeAinsley Harriott explores the country's sweet treats, sampling honey, sugarcane and guava duff. He also meets the makers keeping old-school confectionery alive at Mortimer's Candies, and creates coconut lime creams with a crunchy Bahamian twist.

programme.title: Fletchers' Family Farm
programme.desc: S5 E6Agronomist Ben Clare arrives to check on the farm's oats and maize, while Liz and Kelvin enjoy an unusual date with a visit to local beekeepers. There is also a farewell as bull Ezra's time on the farm comes to an end and Kelvin takes him to market in the hope of finding him a new home.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E1 — OrkneyJames goes on a culinary road trip around the UK and kicks off his travels in the Orkneys, where he is joined by fellow chef Nick Nairn. He shops for hand-dived scallops, before setting up his mobile kitchen in Stromness harbour to make barbecue scallops with black pudding, apple and hazelnut butter. He also meets the owner of a unique herd of sheep in the remote island of North Ronaldsay.

programme.title: Fletchers' Family Farm

In the future, after the nuclear network SkyNet has destroyed most of humanity, John Connor is leading the human resistance fightback. Their plight is complicated, however, by the arrival of the mysterious Marcus Wright, a stranger whose purpose is unclear.

programme.title: English Football League Highlights
programme.desc: S5 E18 — 14/11/2026Action from the latest matches, including Stockport County v Reading at Edgeley Park and Wigan Athletic v Barnsley at The Brick Community Stadium in League One.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: S9 E2Geordie receives a call about a dead body at the River View Hotel but when he goes to investigate, Will and Bonnie discover a baby abandoned inside the church wrapped in a blanket from the same hotel. Ernie leads the pair to believe the baby was abandoned by a school girl. Geordie is shocked and upset to hear Will and Bonnie are thinking of leaving Grantchester.

programme.title: Ainsley's Taste of the Bahamas
programme.desc: S1 E2 — From Farm to TableAinsley Harriott explores the Bahamas' home-grown side as he finds out how to grow salad vegetables without soil at Blue Fields, picks ingredients straight from the trees at Chiccharney Farms and discovers the magic of the mangroves. Once back in his beachside kitchen, Ainsley proceeds to cook a whole snapper.

programme.title: Ainsley's Taste of the Bahamas
programme.desc: S1 E3 — Sweet Island LifeAinsley Harriott explores the country's sweet treats, sampling honey, sugarcane and guava duff. He also meets the makers keeping old-school confectionery alive at Mortimer's Candies, and creates coconut lime creams with a crunchy Bahamian twist.

programme.title: Fletchers' Family Farm
programme.desc: S5 E6Agronomist Ben Clare arrives to check on the farm's oats and maize, while Liz and Kelvin enjoy an unusual date with a visit to local beekeepers. There is also a farewell as bull Ezra's time on the farm comes to an end and Kelvin takes him to market in the hope of finding him a new home.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E1 — OrkneyJames goes on a culinary road trip around the UK and kicks off his travels in the Orkneys, where he is joined by fellow chef Nick Nairn. He shops for hand-dived scallops, before setting up his mobile kitchen in Stromness harbour to make barbecue scallops with black pudding, apple and hazelnut butter. He also meets the owner of a unique herd of sheep in the remote island of North Ronaldsay.

programme.title: James Martin's Saturday Morning
programme.desc: S9 E35James is joined by actress Shelley Conn, who is starring in ITV1's Adultery. The comedian and travel writer Dom Joly is also in the house, with chefs Sally Abe and Glynn Purnell. James cooks Thai green curry and Spanish tapas.

programme.title: Fletchers' Family Farm

programme.desc: S1 E30 — Scotland v AustraliaScotland v Australia (Kick-off 3.10pm). Jill Douglas presents coverage of the Northern Hemisphere Series match at Scottish Gas Murrayfield. programme.title: I'm a Celebrity - How to Survive the Jungle
programme.desc: I'm a Celebrity...How to Survive the JungleAnt and Dec present hints and tongue-in-cheek tips for celebrities to help survive not only the jungle and camp life, but also campmates and their assortment of annoying habits. They also revisit some of the most memorable moments in the programme's history, drawing on a quarter of a century of terrifying trials and camp chaos to arm the next bunch of unsuspecting celebrities with an arsenal of must-have jungle hacks.

programme.title: UEFA Nations League Live
programme.desc: S2 E6 — Spain v EnglandSpain v England (Kick-off 7.45pm). Mark Pougatch presents all the action from both teams' final match in Group A3, held at Riyadh Air Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid. The teams last met in the opening round of fixtures in September, when world champions Spain fought back from 2-1 down to claim a 3-2 win at Wembley Stadium. It was the first meeting between the nations since the UEFA Euro 2024 final in Berlin, which the Spaniards won 2-1, but the Three Lions will be hopeful of avoiding a third defeat in a row to Luis de la Fuente's men, having been in good form since their loss in London. With commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon, analysis from Roy Keane and Ian Wright, and reports by Gabriel Clarke.

programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the Government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels and this undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp in East Sussex now housing asylum seekers. programme.title: UEFA Nations League Live
programme.desc: S2 E6 — Spain v EnglandSpain v England (Kick-off 7.45pm). Mark Pougatch presents all the action from both teams' final match in Group A3, held at Riyadh Air Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid. The teams last met in the opening round of fixtures in September, when world champions Spain fought back from 2-1 down to claim a 3-2 win at Wembley Stadium. It was the first meeting between the nations since the UEFA Euro 2024 final in Berlin, which the Spaniards won 2-1, but the Three Lions will be hopeful of avoiding a third defeat in a row to Luis de la Fuente's men, having been in good form since their loss in London. With commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon, analysis from Roy Keane and Ian Wright, and reports by Gabriel Clarke.

programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the Government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels and this undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp in East Sussex now housing asylum seekers. The programme investigates conditions inside the site, finding how systemically poor welfare checks are having serious consequences, and also examines the local community's response to asylum seekers being housed in the town.

programme.title: Nations Championship
programme.desc: S1 E30 — Scotland v AustraliaScotland v Australia (Kick-off 3.10pm). Jill Douglas presents coverage of the Northern Hemisphere Series match at Scottish Gas Murrayfield. Scotland have an excellent recent record against the Wallabies, winning four of the last five meetings between the sides. The most recent encounter saw them prevail 27-13 here two years ago, with four different players scoring tries for the victors. With commentary by Miles Harrison and Johnnie Beattie, analysis from John Barclay, Greig Laidlaw, and George Gregan, and reports by Lee McKenzie.

programme.title: I'm a Celebrity - How to Survive the Jungle
programme.desc: I'm a Celebrity...How to Survive the JungleAnt and Dec present hints and tongue-in-cheek tips for celebrities to help survive not only the jungle and camp life, but also campmates and their assortment of annoying habits. They also revisit some of the most memorable moments in the programme's history, drawing on a quarter of a century of terrifying trials and camp chaos to arm the next bunch of unsuspecting celebrities with an arsenal of must-have jungle hacks.

programme.title: UEFA Nations League Live
programme.desc: S2 E6 — Spain v EnglandSpain v England (Kick-off 7.45pm). Mark Pougatch presents all the action from both teams' final match in Group A3, held at Riyadh Air Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid. The teams last met in the opening round of fixtures in September, when world champions Spain fought back from 2-1 down to claim a 3-2 win at Wembley Stadium. It was the first meeting between the nations since the UEFA Euro 2024 final in Berlin, which the Spaniards won 2-1, but the Three Lions will be hopeful of avoiding a third defeat in a row to Luis de la Fuente's men, having been in good form since their loss in London. With commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon, analysis from Roy Keane and Ian Wright, and reports by Gabriel Clarke.

programme.title: Inside the Asylum Camp
programme.desc: Mass accommodation sites are central to the Government's plan to end the use of asylum hotels and this undercover investigation goes inside Crowborough, a former military training camp in East Sussex now housing asylum seekers. programme.desc: E1Nazi Germany boasted that its locomotives were faster and more innovative. This programme examines that claim by looking at these ‘flying trains’.
